review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read its dependencies: exists_finite_disk_collar, outsideDisks, isOpen_outsideDisks, closedRoundDisk, squaredLength, polygonal_replacement_with_spurs and path_near_endpoints. Plane is ℝ × ℝ, and squaredLength is defined on coordinates. Generalising the ambient space would mean redoing the whole Crossing development, so I did not propose that. The one useful generalisation I found is a weaker disjointness hypothesis. The target uses `hd` only through exists_finite_disk_collar, and that lemma uses it only once, to show the endpoint is outside every other disk (FiniteDiskCollar.lean, hxV, line 42). The `Finite` and DecidableEq remarks are secondary. Compilation was not tested, and the proposed signatures are unchecked. The only caller I found is SimultaneousExteriorArcs.lean, and I did not read its hypotheses in full.

findings.excerpt: (hd : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (closedRoundDisk (z i) r) (closedRoundDisk (z j) r))
findings.problem: The theorem assumes all the closed disks are pairwise disjoint. Its proof uses that only through exists_finite_disk_collar, and there only to show the endpoint lies strictly outside every other disk. That is `x ∈ closedRoundDisk (z k) r` combined with `hd k j` to get `r^2 < squaredLength (x - z j)` for j ≠ k (FiniteDiskCollar.lean line 42). So the theorem only needs two endpoint facts: a is outside every disk z j with j ≠ k, and b is outside every disk z j with j ≠ l. The global hypothesis is much stronger. It excludes configurations with overlapping disks whose endpoint circles still avoid the other disks. Nothing in the argument needs the interior of the disks to be disjoint.
findings.proposed_change: First weaken the collar lemma. Replace its `hd` with `(hxo : ∀ j, j ≠ k → r^2 < squaredLength (x - z j))`. Then `hxV` becomes `⟨hxu, Set.mem_iInter.mpr (fun j => hxo j.val j.property)⟩`. Then replace `hd` in the target with `(hka : ∀ j, j ≠ k → r^2 < squaredLength (a - z j)) (hlb : ∀ j, j ≠ l → r^2 < squaredLength (b - z j))` and pass these to the two collar calls. Keep a one-line corollary or helper that derives these hypotheses from the pairwise-disjointness `hd`, so SimultaneousExteriorArcs.lean keeps working. The same edit could also change `[Fintype ι]` to `[Finite ι]`, because isOpen_outsideDisks and isOpen_iInter_of_finite only need finiteness. `[DecidableEq ι]` does not appear to be used in the proof.
findings.benefit: The result then applies whenever the endpoints lie outside the other disks, with no global disjointness required. A reader can also see exactly which geometric facts the replacement depends on. The existing pairwise-disjoint case is recovered by the corollary.

evidence.excerpt: exact Set.disjoint_left.mp (hd k j.val (Ne.symm j.property)) (show x ∈ closedRoundDisk (z k) r from hx.le) hh
